title: `Vat.frob` allows debt increase when `dink >= 0 && dart > 0` bypasses ceiling check via `either` short-circuit — actually safe, but `fork` lacks `live` check enabling post-shutdown CDP migration
impact: `Vat.frob` correctly requires `live == 1`, and `grab` is `auth`-gated. However **`Vat.fork` has no `live` check**. After `End.cage()` freezes the system, `fork` still allows moving collateral and debt between urns (with consent). This lets sophisticated actors **rearrange CDP positions after prices are frozen but before `skim`**, potentially moving collateral out of an urn that would be `skim`med into one that has already been `skim`med (or into `free`-eligible state), distorting the `gap` shortfall calculation and the final `fix` prices. Specifically: `skim` is callable by anyone per-urn; an attacker can `fork` collateral from an un-skimmed unsafe urn into a fresh urn, then `free` it after `art == 0` — but `free` requires `art == 0`, so the debt must move too. The exploit requires both parties' consent (`wish`), so this is primarily a **griefing/settlement-integrity** vector between cooperating parties, but it breaks the assumption in `thaw()` that "all under-collateralised CDPs are processed."
